title: Flip Signs k Times for the Biggest Sum
statement:
You get an integer array nums and a number k. A flip picks one index i and replaces nums[i] with −nums[i].

You must make exactly k flips. The same index may be flipped more than once. Return the largest possible sum of the array afterwards.

examples.why: Flip −5 and −3. The third flip must go somewhere: on the 1 it costs 2, on the 3 it would cost 6. 5 + 3 − 1 = 7.
Flip −2 and −1. The other three flips all go to the 0, which changes nothing. 0 + 1 + 2 = 3.

hints: Which single flip helps the sum the most?
Flipping the most negative value is always best. Once no negatives are left, what is the cheapest way to spend the remaining flips?
Two flips on the same index cancel out. So only the parity of the leftover flips matters: if it is odd, one flip lands on the value with the smallest absolute value.

explain.intuition:
Flipping a negative value −x adds 2x to the sum, so turn the most negative values positive first, smallest first. Sorting the array lines them up.

When the negatives run out (or the flips do), any leftover flips come in pairs that cancel on the same index. Only the leftover parity matters. With an even number left, nothing changes. With an odd number left, one value must end up negative, and the cheapest choice is the value with the smallest absolute value, which costs 2 · min|nums[i]|. That value may be one you just flipped, which is why you take the minimum over the whole updated array, not just the remaining positives. A zero makes the last flip free.
steps: Walk from the left: while k > 0 and the value is negative, flip it and decrease k.
Compute the sum and the smallest absolute value in the array.
If k is odd, subtract 2 · smallest. Return the sum.
pitfalls: Spending the leftover flip on the next value in sorted order instead of the smallest absolute value. In [-5, -3, 1] with k = 3, flipping 3 back gives 3 instead of 7.
Flipping a positive value when k is even, instead of letting the flips cancel.
Ignoring zeros: a 0 absorbs any number of leftover flips for free.

solutions.title: Flip the current minimum k times
solutions.idea: Each flip goes to the smallest value at that moment. Correct, but a linear scan per flip.

solutions.title: Sort, flip negatives, settle the parity
solutions.idea: Flip negatives from the most negative up. Leftover flips cancel in pairs; an odd one lands on the smallest absolute value.

followups: Values are limited to [−100, 100]. How does a counting array remove the sort and make it O(n + 200)?
Each index may be flipped at most once. What changes?
lcTitle: Maximize Sum Of Array After K Negations
